offers_products.reason: It leases real estate and sells no manufactured goods or software. Property sales are only capital recycling.

offers_services.reason: As a REIT, it owns, manages and leases office and dedicated-use properties to tenants. The brief counts REITs as services.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Tenants are corporations, medical institutions and government. No households lease the properties.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Tenants include Bank of America, Brown University Health, government and corporate occupiers under net leases.

recurring_revenue.reason: Rent from single-tenant net leases with multi-year terms is recurring lease revenue.

cyclical_demand.reason: Long-term net leases to investment-grade tenants (Bank of America, Brown University Health) make revenue contractual and fairly stable.

big_ticket.reason: Tenants pay recurring rent under long-term net leases, not a large one-off purchase.

people_delivered.reason: Revenue comes from rent on owned buildings, not from staff time or skill.

large_customers.reason: Tenants are mainly large creditworthy corporations and institutions; about 69% of rent comes from investment-grade tenants such as Bank of America.

asset_heavy.reason: REIT owning 57 office and dedicated-use properties across 26 states; growth requires acquiring and investing in buildings.

notes: Orion Properties is the office REIT spun off from Realty Income. The answers rely on the website text and general knowledge.
